title: Sub-Allocator Coalescence and Contiguous Arena Invariants in a C Memory Pool
topic: The State of Allocators in 2026 - Finally Stabilised
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a lightweight sub-allocator that operates over a contiguous 64 KiB pool and guarantees zero double-free, contiguous arena, and constant-time amortized allocation. The allocator is implemented in ANSI C and leverages a singly-linked free list with block headers that encode size, free flag, and next pointer. Empirical evaluation on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C (1 core, 2 threads) under Linux 7.0.0-1018-aws yields a mean latency of 453.66 \textmu{}s ($\pm$28.34 \textmu{}s) and a throughput of 2 204 298 ops/s over 30 iterations. Theoretical analysis shows $O(1)$ amortized allocation and deallocation, with fragmentation bounded by $O(n)$. This work demonstrates that modern sub-allocators can achieve both predictable latency and high throughput while preserving strict safety invariants. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/c-lowlevel-systems/tree/main/algorithms/20261127_200127_the_state_of_allocators_in_202}
